type: Editorial review of the revision-3 contact sheets (one frame per beat), full-size checks of the scan line, chart, word highlight and crossfade, and frame-to-frame measurements of the rendered canvas. Scores evaluate the creative; they are not measured campaign conversion rates.

changes.change: Headlines share one 106 px size (hook 118 px); on-screen text is at least 30 px, including the footer and eyebrow labels; the active caption word is cyan on navy.

A 0.3 s ease-in-out crossfade replaces the hard cut; the scan line now runs inside the fiscal note; the chart has dashed guide lines; the trend-line peak is no longer clipped; all icons come from one stroke set.
Word highlight uses the narration's word boundaries for 17 of 24 captions; the approved AAC track is copied without re-encoding.

findings.Hook: The question Fila no caixa? and the POS illustration are visible at frame zero; the headline is 118 px, still the largest on screen, so the hook keeps its weight.
findings.Readability: One headline size across scenes, a 30 px minimum for on-screen text and high-contrast captions. The active caption word is cyan on navy, about 7:1. The caption band, progress bar and logo badge keep their approved positions, so overlap with the platform UI in the bottom and top bands stays a known limitation, documented in the README.
findings.Motion Quality: The crossfade spreads the scene change over nine frames. The largest frame-to-frame change at the eight cuts fell from 40.5 to 15.3 levels per channel. The scan line sweeps inside the receipt, the chart has guide lines, the trend-line peak is complete, and the icons share one stroke width.
findings.Brand Accuracy: The official logo and the approved palette are unchanged. The icon set is Lucide (ISC licence), drawn in brand purple on light-cyan discs for contrast. Fonts are unchanged.
findings.Sound Sync: The approved AAC track is copied as-is. Word timing comes from the narration for 17 of 24 captions. The other seven captions spell brand names in the voice (éfe pê dê vê, frenti ponto com ponto bê érre), so their highlight is spread across the caption window by character and can lead or lag the speech by a fraction of a second.
